.\compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-b-iter1.md:5292:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3592:.\_archive\compact_v3\ship\chat.ipynb:35:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Action | How |\n|--------|-----|\n| **Send message** | Type in input box, press Send |\n| **Stop agent** | Click Stop button |\n| **Check cost** | Type `/cost` |\n| **Code review** | Type `/review filename.py` |\n| **Explain code** | Type `/explain filename.py` |\n| **Generate tests** | Type `/test filename.py` |\n| **Verify project** | Type `/verify` |\n| **Apply standards** | Type `/standards filename.py` |\n| **Revert file** | Type `/revert filename.py` or `/revert all` |\n| **Compact context** | Click Compact button (or auto at 80%) |\n| **Clean traces** | Click Clean button (removes audit/snapshots, keeps sessions) |\n| **Save/Load** | Save button (auto-saves each message) / Session dropdown + Load |\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\n| Task | What to type |\n|------|-------------|\n| Read a file | \"Read app.py\" |\n| Find files | \"Find all Python files in this project\" |\n| Fix a bug | \"Read app.py, find the bug, and fix it\" |\n| Create chart | \"Create a bar chart from sales.csv showing revenue by product\" |\n| Create report | \"Create a Word report summarizing the data in results.csv\" |\n| Run command | \"Run git status\" |\n| Analyze image | \"Look at screenshot.png and describe what you see\" |\n| Search code | \"Find where authentication is handled in this codebase\" |\n\n## 22 Tools\n\n| Category | Tools | Approval? |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. Context auto-compacts at 80% usage (prune old tool outputs, then LLM summarize if needed)\n\n## Token Overhead Per API Call\n\n| Component | Tokens |\n|-----------|--------|\n| System prompt | ~1,200 |\n| Tool schemas | ~1,800 (lazy-load: ~1,200 for coding tasks) |\n| Bedrock overhead | ~346 |\n| **Total per call** | **~3,350** |\n\n## Session Management\n\n| Feature | How |\n|---------|-----|\n| **Auto-save** | Every message auto-saves (messages, todos, metadata) |\n| **Load session** | Session dropdown + Load button |\n| **New session** | New button (clears all state) |\n| **Checkpoints** | `/checkpoint name` (saves snapshot, max 50) |\n\n## Commands vs Skills\n\n| Method | How | Depth | Persists? |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. Commands cover the same categories with less detail.\n\n## Config\n\nDefault config is set in Cell 3 (before launch). Change model, temperature, thinking mode anytime in the chatbot UI during use.\n\nKey security settings (Cell 3):\n- `aws_bedrock_only = True` \u2014 blocks all AWS except Bedrock\n- `session_cost_limit = 1.0` \u2014 max $1 per session\n- `require_tool_approval = True` \u2014 approve/deny before execution"

.\compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-t-iter1.md:484:compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-b-iter1.md:5292:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3592:.\_archive\compact_v3\ship\chat.ipynb:35:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Action | How |\n|--------|-----|\n| **Send message** | Type in input box, press Send |\n| **Stop agent** | Click Stop button |\n| **Check cost** | Type `/cost` |\n| **Code review** | Type `/review filename.py` |\n| **Explain code** | Type `/explain filename.py` |\n| **Generate tests** | Type `/test filename.py` |\n| **Verify project** | Type `/verify` |\n| **Apply standards** | Type `/standards filename.py` |\n| **Revert file** | Type `/revert filename.py` or `/revert all` |\n| **Compact context** | Click Compact button (or auto at 80%) |\n| **Clean traces** | Click Clean button (removes audit/snapshots, keeps sessions) |\n| **Save/Load** | Save button (auto-saves each message) / Session dropdown + Load |\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\n| Task | What to type |\n|------|-------------|\n| Read a file | \"Read app.py\" |\n| Find files | \"Find all Python files in this project\" |\n| Fix a bug | \"Read app.py, find the bug, and fix it\" |\n| Create chart | \"Create a bar chart from sales.csv showing revenue by product\" |\n| Create report | \"Create a Word report summarizing the data in results.csv\" |\n| Run command | \"Run git status\" |\n| Analyze image | \"Look at screenshot.png and describe what you see\" |\n| Search code | \"Find where authentication is handled in this codebase\" |\n\n## 22 Tools\n\n| Category | Tools | Approval? |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. Context auto-compacts at 80% usage (prune old tool outputs, then LLM summarize if needed)\n\n## Token Overhead Per API Call\n\n| Component | Tokens |\n|-----------|--------|\n| System prompt | ~1,200 |\n| Tool schemas | ~1,800 (lazy-load: ~1,200 for coding tasks) |\n| Bedrock overhead | ~346 |\n| **Total per call** | **~3,350** |\n\n## Session Management\n\n| Feature | How |\n|---------|-----|\n| **Auto-save** | Every message auto-saves (messages, todos, metadata) |\n| **Load session** | Session dropdown + Load button |\n| **New session** | New button (clears all state) |\n| **Checkpoints** | `/checkpoint name` (saves snapshot, max 50) |\n\n## Commands vs Skills\n\n| Method | How | Depth | Persists? |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. Commands cover the same categories with less detail.\n\n## Config\n\nDefault config is set in Cell 3 (before launch). Change model, temperature, thinking mode anytime in the chatbot UI during use.\n\nKey security settings (Cell 3):\n- `aws_bedrock_only = True` \u2014 blocks all AWS except Bedrock\n- `session_cost_limit = 1.0` \u2014 max $1 per session\n- `require_tool_approval = True` \u2014 approve/deny before execution"

|\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. (c) **Wave 6 gap #8 — tool-vs-skill precedence** (PS_Plan_Edge_Cases_Thinking.md #93 / W6_multi_file_tasks.md:327-371): v5 disposition is **tools win for offline SageMaker / Bedrock-only deployments** because Block T's document tools (create_word, create_excel, create_chart, etc.) are zero-network-dependency and run inside the agent process; bundled skills (Runnable's debug, remember, etc.) are designed for the network-rich Anthropic-API-direct world and may reference tools that v5 doesn't ship (constraint #9 + #10). The model resolves a request by: (1) check direct tool registry first; (2) if no tool fits, check active skill body; (3) only suggest /skill use <name> when the user's task explicitly maps to a skill's CSO description. Block I lands the bundled debug + remember skills but they are auxiliary surfaces, not replacements for tools. ADR-029. | NEEDS-ADAPTATION per Wave 5-DEEP §Block F2: Runnable's tokenBudget tracks turn-output-tokens vs a user-set token budget parsed from the message text ("+500k"); v5 reuses the existing IterationBudget surface (counts turns) — same semantic, fewer surfaces, matches scenario #21 wording. DIMINISHING_THRESHOLD adapted from 500 tokens → 2 iterations. Cost-cap halt added (Wave 6 NLT row #21): even when iter_used < 90%, if session_cost ≥ session_cost_limit → halt. Sub-agents always halt (parent-only auto-continuation, matches Runnable agentId early-out at tokenBudget.ts:51). Default-OFF opt-in (Wave 6 NLT row #21 contract). Tracker reset to None at run() entry — never leaks state across user messages. F2 logic best-effort wrapped in try/except so it never blocks normal end_turn. Lock tests: 14 in test_block_f2.py — 7 pure-function (continue-under-90 / stop-at-90 / cost-cap / subagent / diminishing-after-3 / no-budget / message-format) + 3 TEST_DESIGN-named (auto_continue_at_under_90pct / blocks_at_90pct / respects_cost_cap) + 4 behavioral locks (default-off-no-continuation, diminishing-returns-end-to-end, subagent-no-auto-continue, tracker-resets-between-runs). ADR-028. |

.\compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-t-iter1.md:808:compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-i-iter2.md:2422:compact_v5/_status\codex_reviews\block-b-iter1.md:5292:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3592:.\_archive\compact_v3\ship\chat.ipynb:35:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Action | How |\n|--------|-----|\n| **Send message** | Type in input box, press Send |\n| **Stop agent** | Click Stop button |\n| **Check cost** | Type `/cost` |\n| **Code review** | Type `/review filename.py` |\n| **Explain code** | Type `/explain filename.py` |\n| **Generate tests** | Type `/test filename.py` |\n| **Verify project** | Type `/verify` |\n| **Apply standards** | Type `/standards filename.py` |\n| **Revert file** | Type `/revert filename.py` or `/revert all` |\n| **Compact context** | Click Compact button (or auto at 80%) |\n| **Clean traces** | Click Clean button (removes audit/snapshots, keeps sessions) |\n| **Save/Load** | Save button (auto-saves each message) / Session dropdown + Load |\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\n| Task | What to type |\n|------|-------------|\n| Read a file | \"Read app.py\" |\n| Find files | \"Find all Python files in this project\" |\n| Fix a bug | \"Read app.py, find the bug, and fix it\" |\n| Create chart | \"Create a bar chart from sales.csv showing revenue by product\" |\n| Create report | \"Create a Word report summarizing the data in results.csv\" |\n| Run command | \"Run git status\" |\n| Analyze image | \"Look at screenshot.png and describe what you see\" |\n| Search code | \"Find where authentication is handled in this codebase\" |\n\n## 22 Tools\n\n| Category | Tools | Approval? |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. Context auto-compacts at 80% usage (prune old tool outputs, then LLM summarize if needed)\n\n## Token Overhead Per API Call\n\n| Component | Tokens |\n|-----------|--------|\n| System prompt | ~1,200 |\n| Tool schemas | ~1,800 (lazy-load: ~1,200 for coding tasks) |\n| Bedrock overhead | ~346 |\n| **Total per call** | **~3,350** |\n\n## Session Management\n\n| Feature | How |\n|---------|-----|\n| **Auto-save** | Every message auto-saves (messages, todos, metadata) |\n| **Load session** | Session dropdown + Load button |\n| **New session** | New button (clears all state) |\n| **Checkpoints** | `/checkpoint name` (saves snapshot, max 50) |\n\n## Commands vs Skills\n\n| Method | How | Depth | Persists? |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. Commands cover the same categories with less detail.\n\n## Config\n\nDefault config is set in Cell 3 (before launch). Change model, temperature, thinking mode anytime in the chatbot UI during use.\n\nKey security settings (Cell 3):\n- `aws_bedrock_only = True` \u2014 blocks all AWS except Bedrock\n- `session_cost_limit = 1.0` \u2014 max $1 per session\n- `require_tool_approval = True` \u2014 approve/deny before execution"

Sub-agents always halt (parent-only auto-continuation, matches Runnable agentId early-out at tokenBudget.ts:51). Default-OFF opt-in (Wave 6 NLT row #21 contract). .\compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-t-iter1.md:1183:compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3592:.\_archive\compact_v3\ship\chat.ipynb:35:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Action | How |\n|--------|-----|\n| **Send message** | Type in input box, press Send |\n| **Stop agent** | Click Stop button |\n| **Check cost** | Type `/cost` |\n| **Code review** | Type `/review filename.py` |\n| **Explain code** | Type `/explain filename.py` |\n| **Generate tests** | Type `/test filename.py` |\n| **Verify project** | Type `/verify` |\n| **Apply standards** | Type `/standards filename.py` |\n| **Revert file** | Type `/revert filename.py` or `/revert all` |\n| **Compact context** | Click Compact button (or auto at 80%) |\n| **Clean traces** | Click Clean button (removes audit/snapshots, keeps sessions) |\n| **Save/Load** | Save button (auto-saves each message) / Session dropdown + Load |\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\n| Task | What to type |\n|------|-------------|\n| Read a file | \"Read app.py\" |\n| Find files | \"Find all Python files in this project\" |\n| Fix a bug | \"Read app.py, find the bug, and fix it\" |\n| Create chart | \"Create a bar chart from sales.csv showing revenue by product\" |\n| Create report | \"Create a Word report summarizing the data in results.csv\" |\n| Run command | \"Run git status\" |\n| Analyze image | \"Look at screenshot.png and describe what you see\" |\n| Search code | \"Find where authentication is handled in this codebase\" |\n\n## 22 Tools\n\n| Category | Tools | Approval? |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. Context auto-compacts at 80% usage (prune old tool outputs, then LLM summarize if needed)\n\n## Token Overhead Per API Call\n\n| Component | Tokens |\n|-----------|--------|\n| System prompt | ~1,200 |\n| Tool schemas | ~1,800 (lazy-load: ~1,200 for coding tasks) |\n| Bedrock overhead | ~346 |\n| **Total per call** | **~3,350** |\n\n## Session Management\n\n| Feature | How |\n|---------|-----|\n| **Auto-save** | Every message auto-saves (messages, todos, metadata) |\n| **Load session** | Session dropdown + Load button |\n| **New session** | New button (clears all state) |\n| **Checkpoints** | `/checkpoint name` (saves snapshot, max 50) |\n\n## Commands vs Skills\n\n| Method | How | Depth | Persists? |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. Commands cover the same categories with less detail.\n\n## Config\n\nDefault config is set in Cell 3 (before launch). Change model, temperature, thinking mode anytime in the chatbot UI during use.\n\nKey security settings (Cell 3):\n- `aws_bedrock_only = True` \u2014 blocks all AWS except Bedrock\n- `session_cost_limit = 1.0` \u2014 max $1 per session\n- `require_tool_approval = True` \u2014 approve/deny before execution"

(b) **Wave 6 row #93** (`PORT_LOG enumerates skills/verify/ as bundled`): closed via existing PORT_LOG #029 (Phase-10 byte-for-byte copy of 10 v4 production skills including verify). Block I makes no change to the bundled set; Phase-10 row is the canonical evidence. (c) **Wave 6 gap #8 — tool-vs-skill precedence** (PS_Plan_Edge_Cases_Thinking.md #93 / W6_multi_file_tasks.md:327-371): v5 disposition is **tools win for offline SageMaker / Bedrock-only deployments** because Block T's document tools (create_word, create_excel, create_chart, etc.) are zero-network-dependency and run inside the agent process; bundled skills (Runnable's debug, remember, etc.) are designed for the network-rich Anthropic-API-direct world and may reference tools that v5 doesn't ship (constraint #9 + #10). The model resolves a request by: (1) check direct tool registry first; (2) if no tool fits, check active skill body; (3) only suggest /skill use <name> when the user's task explicitly maps to a skill's CSO description. Block I lands the bundled debug + remember skills but they are auxiliary surfaces, not replacements for tools. ADR-029. | NEEDS-ADAPTATION per Wave 5-DEEP §Block F2: Runnable's tokenBudget tracks turn-output-tokens vs a user-set token budget parsed from the message text ("+500k"); v5 reuses the existing IterationBudget surface (counts turns) — same semantic, fewer surfaces, matches scenario #21 wording. DIMINISHING_THRESHOLD adapted from 500 tokens → 2 iterations. Cost-cap halt added (Wave 6 NLT row #21): even when iter_used < 90%, if session_cost ≥ session_cost_limit → halt. Sub-agents always halt (parent-only auto-continuation, matches Runnable agentId early-out at tokenBudget.ts:51). Default-OFF opt-in (Wave 6 NLT row #21 contract). Tracker reset to None at run() entry — never leaks state across user messages. F2 logic best-effort wrapped in try/except so it never blocks normal end_turn. Lock tests: 14 in test_block_f2.py — 7 pure-function (continue-under-90 / stop-at-90 / cost-cap / subagent / diminishing-after-3 / no-budget / message-format) + 3 TEST_DESIGN-named (auto_continue_at_under_90pct / blocks_at_90pct / respects_cost_cap) + 4 behavioral locks (default-off-no-continuation, diminishing-returns-end-to-end, subagent-no-auto-continue, tracker-resets-between-runs). ADR-028. |

.\compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-m-iter1.md:3371:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3825:.\_archive\compact\chat.ipynb:172:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\nTry these prompts to test the agent:\n\n| Task | Example Prompt |\n|------|----------------|\n| **Explore** | \"List files in this directory\" |\n| **Read** | \"Read the README.md file\" |\n| **Search** | \"Find all Python files with test in the name\" |\n| **Semantic Search** | \"Find where authentication is handled\" |\n| **Edit** | \"Add a comment to the top of file.py\" |\n| **Execute** | \"Run git status\" |\n| **Create Excel** | \"Create an Excel file with employee data\" |\n| **Create Word** | \"Write a project summary document\" |\n| **Create PDF** | \"Create a PDF report with table and chart summary\" |\n| **Create Notebook** | \"Create a notebook that loads and analyzes data\" |\n| **Plan** | \"Help me build a REST API with Flask\" |\n\n---\n\n## Capabilities\n\n**22 Tools:**\n- File: `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `glob`, `grep`, `list_dir`\n- Shell: `bash`\n- Python: `python_exec`\n- Documents: `create_word`, `create_excel`, `create_markdown`, `create_notebook`, `create_pdf`\n- Charts: `create_chart` (inline display)\n- Vision: `view_image`\n- Search: `semantic_search` (AI-powered code search)\n- Skills/MCP: `skill_list`, `skill_read`, `mcp_call`, `subagent_run`\n- Planning: `todo_write`, `todo_read`\n\n**Security:**\n- Workspace boundary enforcement\n- Secret detection (API keys, passwords, tokens)\n- Dangerous command blocking and restricted execution mode\n- Tool approval is configurable via UI `Require Approval` (default OFF in SageMaker)\n- Audit logging and session persistence"

.\compact_v5\_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3592:.\_archive\compact_v3\ship\chat.ipynb:35:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Action | How |\n|--------|-----|\n| **Send message** | Type in input box, press Send |\n| **Stop agent** | Click Stop button |\n| **Check cost** | Type `/cost` |\n| **Code review** | Type `/review filename.py` |\n| **Explain code** | Type `/explain filename.py` |\n| **Generate tests** | Type `/test filename.py` |\n| **Verify project** | Type `/verify` |\n| **Apply standards** | Type `/standards filename.py` |\n| **Revert file** | Type `/revert filename.py` or `/revert all` |\n| **Compact context** | Click Compact button (or auto at 80%) |\n| **Clean traces** | Click Clean button (removes audit/snapshots, keeps sessions) |\n| **Save/Load** | Save button (auto-saves each message) / Session dropdown + Load |\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\n| Task | What to type |\n|------|-------------|\n| Read a file | \"Read app.py\" |\n| Find files | \"Find all Python files in this project\" |\n| Fix a bug | \"Read app.py, find the bug, and fix it\" |\n| Create chart | \"Create a bar chart from sales.csv showing revenue by product\" |\n| Create report | \"Create a Word report summarizing the data in results.csv\" |\n| Run command | \"Run git status\" |\n| Analyze image | \"Look at screenshot.png and describe what you see\" |\n| Search code | \"Find where authentication is handled in this codebase\" |\n\n## 22 Tools\n\n| Category | Tools | Approval? |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. Context auto-compacts at 80% usage (prune old tool outputs, then LLM summarize if needed)\n\n## Token Overhead Per API Call\n\n| Component | Tokens |\n|-----------|--------|\n| System prompt | ~1,200 |\n| Tool schemas | ~1,800 (lazy-load: ~1,200 for coding tasks) |\n| Bedrock overhead | ~346 |\n| **Total per call** | **~3,350** |\n\n## Session Management\n\n| Feature | How |\n|---------|-----|\n| **Auto-save** | Every message auto-saves (messages, todos, metadata) |\n| **Load session** | Session dropdown + Load button |\n| **New session** | New button (clears all state) |\n| **Checkpoints** | `/checkpoint name` (saves snapshot, max 50) |\n\n## Commands vs Skills\n\n| Method | How | Depth | Persists? |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. Commands cover the same categories with less detail.\n\n## Config\n\nDefault config is set in Cell 3 (before launch). Change model, temperature, thinking mode anytime in the chatbot UI during use.\n\nKey security settings (Cell 3):\n- `aws_bedrock_only = True` \u2014 blocks all AWS except Bedrock\n- `session_cost_limit = 1.0` \u2014 max $1 per session\n- `require_tool_approval = True` \u2014 approve/deny before execution"

(a) **I-12 frontmatter parser improvements** (R8 #24, #50): DEFERRED to Block N per ADR-029 §6 (architectural fit — frontmatter expansion lands with Block N's dynamic-section + AGENTS.md infrastructure). (c) **Wave 6 gap #8 — tool-vs-skill precedence** (PS_Plan_Edge_Cases_Thinking.md #93 / W6_multi_file_tasks.md:327-371): v5 disposition is **tools win for offline SageMaker / Bedrock-only deployments** because Block T's document tools (create_word, create_excel, create_chart, etc.) are zero-network-dependency and run inside the agent process; bundled skills (Runnable's debug, remember, etc.) are designed for the network-rich Anthropic-API-direct world and may reference tools that v5 doesn't ship (constraint #9 + #10). Block I lands the bundled debug + remember skills but they are auxiliary surfaces, not replacements for tools. ADR-029. |

.\compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-i-iter2.md:2422:compact_v5/_status\codex_reviews\block-b-iter1.md:5292:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3592:.\_archive\compact_v3\ship\chat.ipynb:35:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Action | How |\n|--------|-----|\n| **Send message** | Type in input box, press Send |\n| **Stop agent** | Click Stop button |\n| **Check cost** | Type `/cost` |\n| **Code review** | Type `/review filename.py` |\n| **Explain code** | Type `/explain filename.py` |\n| **Generate tests** | Type `/test filename.py` |\n| **Verify project** | Type `/verify` |\n| **Apply standards** | Type `/standards filename.py` |\n| **Revert file** | Type `/revert filename.py` or `/revert all` |\n| **Compact context** | Click Compact button (or auto at 80%) |\n| **Clean traces** | Click Clean button (removes audit/snapshots, keeps sessions) |\n| **Save/Load** | Save button (auto-saves each message) / Session dropdown + Load |\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\n| Task | What to type |\n|------|-------------|\n| Read a file | \"Read app.py\" |\n| Find files | \"Find all Python files in this project\" |\n| Fix a bug | \"Read app.py, find the bug, and fix it\" |\n| Create chart | \"Create a bar chart from sales.csv showing revenue by product\" |\n| Create report | \"Create a Word report summarizing the data in results.csv\" |\n| Run command | \"Run git status\" |\n| Analyze image | \"Look at screenshot.png and describe what you see\" |\n| Search code | \"Find where authentication is handled in this codebase\" |\n\n## 22 Tools\n\n| Category | Tools | Approval? |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. Context auto-compacts at 80% usage (prune old tool outputs, then LLM summarize if needed)\n\n## Token Overhead Per API Call\n\n| Component | Tokens |\n|-----------|--------|\n| System prompt | ~1,200 |\n| Tool schemas | ~1,800 (lazy-load: ~1,200 for coding tasks) |\n| Bedrock overhead | ~346 |\n| **Total per call** | **~3,350** |\n\n## Session Management\n\n| Feature | How |\n|---------|-----|\n| **Auto-save** | Every message auto-saves (messages, todos, metadata) |\n| **Load session** | Session dropdown + Load button |\n| **New session** | New button (clears all state) |\n| **Checkpoints** | `/checkpoint name` (saves snapshot, max 50) |\n\n## Commands vs Skills\n\n| Method | How | Depth | Persists? |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. Commands cover the same categories with less detail.\n\n## Config\n\nDefault config is set in Cell 3 (before launch). Change model, temperature, thinking mode anytime in the chatbot UI during use.\n\nKey security settings (Cell 3):\n- `aws_bedrock_only = True` \u2014 blocks all AWS except Bedrock\n- `session_cost_limit = 1.0` \u2014 max $1 per session\n- `require_tool_approval = True` \u2014 approve/deny before execution"

+def test_tool_create_chart_v4_combo_shape(workspace_tmp):

+    shape (sagemaker_agent.py:6194-6214)."""
+    pytest.importorskip("matplotlib")
+    fp = str(workspace_tmp / "combo.png")
+    tool = _find_tool("create_chart")
+    out = tool.execute({
+        "filepath": fp,
+        "chart_type": "combo",
+        "data": {
+            "labels": ["Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"],
+            "bar_values": [10, 20, 15, 25],
+            "line_values": [12, 18, 14, 22],
+            "bar_label": "Revenue",
+            "line_label": "Profit",
+            "line_ylabel": "Profit ($M)",
+        },
+        "title": "Annual Performance",
+    }, context={})
+    assert out.startswith("Wrote "), out
+    assert os.path.isfile(fp)
+
+
+def test_tool_create_chart_filepath_defaults_to_chart_png(workspace_tmp):
+    """Codex iter-4 HIGH lock: v4 defaults filepath to 'chart.png' when
+    omitted (sagemaker_agent.py:6049-6052; schema required=[data])."""
+    pytest.importorskip("matplotlib")

+    cwd = os.getcwd()

+    try:
+        tool = _find_tool("create_chart")
+        out = tool.execute({
+            "chart_type": "bar",
+            "data": {"A": 1, "B": 2},
+        }, context={})
+        assert out.startswith("Wrote "), out
+        # Default filepath = chart.png within workspace.
+        assert "chart.png" in out
+    finally:
+        os.chdir(cwd)
+

Changes merged back on success. Cleanup always runs.</td><td><span class="pill yes">Closed</span></td><td>[CRITICAL] Build mistakes no longer corrupt workspace. Sequential-only (parallel builds skip). Configurable: enable_worktree.</td></tr>
compact_v5/MAIN/agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:764:          <li>Single-file agent is easier to copy into notebooks and managed workspaces.</li>
compact_v5/MAIN/agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:818:          <li><b>Problem observed</b>: Agent launched in a subfolder couldn't find files that lived in the parent git repo. <code>glob "**/name.py"</code> returned <code>No files found</code> even though the file WAS readable via <code>read_file</code> (which walks <code>allowed_paths</code>). The model trusted the negative glob result and gave up.</li>
compact_v5/MAIN/agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:819:          <li><b>Root cause</b>: Four architectural blind spots — (1) agent had no way to know its workspace root, (2) error messages didn't reveal workspace or allowed roots, (3) <code>glob</code> only searched workspace while <code>read_file</code> also searched <code>allowed_paths</code>, (4) no startup announcement.</li>
compact_v5/MAIN/agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:820:          <li><b>Fix 1 — Workspace info in cached prompt</b>: New <code>_build_workspace_info()</code> helper injects <code># Workspace</code> block (Root + Also accessible + path rules) before the <code># === DYNAMIC ===</code> marker in <code>Agent.run()</code>. Cached = zero per-turn cost (~125 tokens one-time).</li>
compact_v5/MAIN/agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:821:          <li><b>Fix 2 — <code>tool_glob</code> fall-through</b>: When workspace search returns empty and no explicit <code>path</code> arg was given, glob retries against every root in <code>SECURITY.allowed_paths</code>. Result lines append <code>[Searched N roots]</code> when fall-through was used.</li>
compact_v5/MAIN/agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:822:          <li><b>Fix 3 — Informative errors</b>: <code>validate_path</code>, <code>tool_read_file</code>, and <code>tool_glob</code> all now include workspace root + allowed roots + a <code>glob "**/filename"</code> or <code>bash find</code> recovery template. The agent self-corrects without user help.</li>
compact_v5/MAIN/agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:824:          <li><b>Verification</b>: Unit test <code>test_v461_path_fix.py</code> — <b>11/11 PASS</b>. Reproduces the exact failure (fresh git repo, workspace in subfolder, target file in parent) and verifies all 4 code paths.</li>
compact_v5/MAIN/agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:826:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Troubleshooting tip:</b> If the agent says "file not found" or glob returns empty, check the <code>[Workspace: ...]</code> line printed at session start. If your target file is outside that path, it must be in an <code>Also accessible</code> root (auto-added: git repo root, SageMaker home). Otherwise add it explicitly via <code>agent_config.json</code> → <code>allowed_paths</code>. Why this matters: before this fix, Sonnet blamed itself for "habit failure" — but the real cause was that the tools gave it no way to know where it was. V4.6.1 closes that blind spot.</p>
compact_v5/MAIN/agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:958:      <p>Think of the system prompt as the agent's job description taped to the monitor. It says things like "be safe", "stay inside the workspace", "use tools correctly", and "format answers clearly". Every turn, the model reads that job description before it decides what to do.</p>
compact_v5/MAIN/agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:982:      <p>A security layer is one checkpoint in a pipeline that checks whether a command is safe to run. V4 has 16 of these, stacked like airport security: Layer -1 blocks catastrophic commands (like "delete everything", 13 patterns) with no override possible. Layers 0-2 check against an allowlist, 75+ dangerous patterns, and network/workspace restrictions. Layers 3-5 validate tool names, arguments, file paths, and user permissions. If ANY layer says "no", the command is blocked. This defense-in-depth approach means even if one layer has a gap, the others catch it.</p>
compact_v5/MAIN/agent\skills\html\references\flowchart_page.html:994:      <p>Every turn, V4 sends the system prompt (instructions, tool definitions, rules) to Bedrock. Without caching, you pay full price for these ~4,000+ tokens every single turn. With caching, Bedrock remembers the prompt from last turn and charges 90% less. The catch: caching only works if the prompt is EXACTLY the same — even changing one character breaks the cache. That's why V4 splits the prompt into a "static" part (instructions, rules — never changes) and a "dynamic" part (workspace info, memory — changes each turn). The static part gets cached. On Haiku, the minimum threshold is 4,096 tokens — V4's rich tool descriptions push past this threshold, activating cache and saving ~$0.19 per session.</p>

  24: def _ask_user_executor(args: Dict[str, Any], context: Optional[Dict] = None) -> str:
  25:     question = str(args.get("question") or "").strip()

  34:     prompt = question
  35:     if options:
  36:         prompt = (
  37:             question
  38:             + "\nOptions:\n"
  39:             + "\n".join(f"  {i+1}. {o}" for i, o in enumerate(options))
  40:         )
  41: 
  42:     # Test/UI hook: caller injects a response provider via context.
  43:     provider = (context or {}).get("ask_user_response_provider")
  44:     if callable(provider):

  48:         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001

  51:     # Live console path: blocks for user input.

**Findings**

MEDIUM: v4 combo shape is detected, but its labels are parsed incorrectly. In [v4_documents.py](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/v4_documents.py:417), `{labels, bar_values, line_values}` misses every explicit parser branch and falls into the generic dict path at lines 436-438, so `labels` becomes `["labels", "bar_values", "line_values", ...]`. The combo renderer then uses those wrong labels at [line 501](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/v4_documents.py:501), [line 506](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/v4_documents.py:506), and [line 510](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/v4_documents.py:510). Fix by parsing the combo shape before the generic dict fallback: when `labels` plus `bar_values`/`line_values` are present, set `labels = data["labels"]` and `values = bar_values`/`values` fallback.

Single-axis combo when `line_ylabel` is omitted is implemented at [v4_documents.py:509](D:/Github/sagemaker-coding-agent/compact_v5/MAIN/agent/tools/v4_documents.py:509). `twinx()` does not leak on successful render because the figure closes at line 542; the broader pre-existing outer-exception path still does not close figures, but I would not block Block T on that.
